scope: Closure of the discussed candidate families and targeted source audit across the project components; not a claim of universal SciPy optimality. All retained measured candidates were implemented and tested.

triage.evidence: Prototype 0.93–0.94x plain SciPy; preserve original dispatch.
Queries, knots and coefficients can change in place; no immutable-input API contract.

triage.candidate: Major-axis and many-small-block sparse stacking shortcut
triage.evidence: Validation cost: major axis 0.68–0.85x prior fastscipy; 20 small blocks 0.46–0.60x; four small blocks only 1.03x.
Earlier round: 1.00–1.07x before adding further guards; prototype removed.
Feasible scalar bounds ~1.08x; active TRF/BVLS ~0.99–1.04x; vector bounds ~0.90–0.97x. Details in optimize.json.
Only ~1.07x before guards and wrapper overhead.
One-ULP difference from NumPy padding/traversal and detrending order; original SciPy path retained.
SciPy batch adapter owns dtype deprecation warnings; original path retained.
Conversion can report signaling-NaN cast events; optimization restricted to validated integer/bool CSR.
DUCC already provides worker controls. An automatic override needs explicit handling of set_workers contexts, alternate backends and shared thread budgets.

triage.candidate: Large dense linear algebra and interpolative routines
triage.evidence: Existing BLAS/LAPACK kernels dominate large operations. New single-factor and triangular dispatch paths cover demonstrated small-call gains.

triage.decision: source-reviewed; no numerical fast-path target established
triage.evidence: File-format parsing/native libraries, filesystem/network activity or simple lookups require workload-specific evidence; no IO or download side effects introduced.
Callbacks, cached weights and stopping/error behavior require workload-specific profiling. Existing numerical-gradient and analytic Rosenbrock paths retained.

unproven_remaining_ideas.status: Require algorithm/kernel work and new profiling; no guaranteed speedup claimed.
Additional precision, FFT-mode and promotion matching needed; existing fallbacks preserved.
Separate dtype/exception semantics and profiling required; existing fallbacks preserved.
Not exhaustively profiled. Public export counts are not counts of guaranteed remaining wins.

retained: Canonical compact integer/bool CSR unweighted Dijkstra omits float64 weight copies; same Rust unit kernel
rejected: Float32 unweighted conversion elimination: could suppress signaling-NaN conversion warnings
Trusting CSR canonical flags: stale after caller mutation; validate actual buffers instead
remaining: New traversal/order algorithms and median labelled reductions require native kernels/build and exact-order validation
Weighted graph kernels already native; no mutable graph/query cache

notes: Small irregular 1-D cumulative Simpson has marginal improvement; retained as the same implementation gives larger gains for long arrays and multiple channels.
Wave 3 adds explicit real-coordinate Simpson and float32/complex64/complex128 uniform Simpson; original eight wave-1 measurements and baseline are preserved.
remaining_opportunities: Complex Simpson with explicit coordinates and exact promoted complex arithmetic
NumPy scalar dx promotion for Simpson
Repeated/mixed-sign irregular grids currently delegated to SciPy

rejected.reason: SciPy batch decorator emits dtype deprecation warning; retain original warning behavior via fallback

remaining: float32 and complex native batch kernels require Rust LAPACK support/build
retained: Single cho_solve and lu_solve call original SciPy nonbatch core, preserving validation and LAPACK arithmetic; no-retry accepted branches
LU checks only RHS finiteness, and pivot ranges are guarded before LAPACK
Typed wrappers retain prior native-batch try/fallback dispatch without stacking another public wrapper
Center of mass now accepts int16 and uint16 through existing exact native sums
Zero-mass sums decline before numpy division so raising seterr handler runs once
rejected: Broad float16 support: SciPy/kernel dtype and warning behavior not matched
remaining: Labelled median and new reducers need native algorithms and summation-order tests
Float32 filtering/interpolation and layouts already handled by existing native paths
Complex filters use SciPy wrappers splitting real/imaginary data to the existing real kernels

rejected_candidates.observations: Scalar feasible ~1.08x; active TRF/BVLS ~0.99–1.04x; vector bounds ~0.90–0.97x versus prior fastscipy.
rejected_candidates.reason: Added validation/allocation/dispatch complexity was not justified; prototype fully reverted.

remaining_opportunities: Numerical-gradient vectorization requires preserving callback order, side effects, and mutation semantics.
Specialized linear-solver kernels would require native work and strict arithmetic validation.

retained: Existing no-retry MatrixLinearOperator sparse vector shortcut now also accepts exact SciPy _AdjointMatrixOperator class
Same stored conjugate-transpose matrix and sparse kernel; namespace/custom-subclass guards unchanged

incremental_prototype.lsmr_vs_previous_fastscipy: 0.98-1.11x; solver arithmetic dominates and timing is noisy

remaining: Block matmat wrappers and additional solver setup need independent profiling
Native sparse kernels remain SciPy; no changed iteration arithmetic

independent_review.result: No actionable witnessed issues; small numeric-payload/spacing/layout probes matched SciPy.

signal_callback_review.finding: Speculative underflow and cold-cache computations could invoke NumPy handlers before retrying SciPy.
signal_callback_review.resolution: All floating-point preflight events become internal FloatingPointError and decline before invoking the original. Full SFT cache construction is included. Raising call/log handlers execute once.
signal_callback_review.validation: 558 signal tests passed; 284 unchanged paired upstream outcomes, 804 fast calls and zero fast errors.
